clue.text: Payment in advance of future production is welcomed by cosmetics expert in recession

definitions.text: Payment in advance of future production

indicators.note: something in recession is going backwards, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
being welcomed by someone means being taken in by them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Estée Lauder founded the cosmetics company bearing her name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cosmetics expert in a downturn is glad of money paid up front for goods not yet made.
explanation.walkthrough: Estée Lauder is the cosmetics expert; the reversed assembly reads LAUISDER backwards. A residual is agreed in the original contract, ahead of any repeat use.
explanation.definitionFit: A residual is a fee paid to a performer for later reuse or repeat screenings of a production.

clue.text: Replants flamboyant trees around square

indicators.note: around means surrounding the other piece
flamboyant suggests showy wildness, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A gardener replants showy trees round a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flamboyant' makes REETS from TREES, and 'around' puts it round S. 'Flamboyant' is also a tree name, which feeds the gardening picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset seedlings is to set them in the ground again, putting them in fresh positions.

clue.text: Students elevated in error

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means lifted upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: pupils are students

explanation.surface: Students were promoted by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a careless mistake.

clue.text: Wife evenly adjusts heating system

indicators.note: evenly means taking the even-numbered letters, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: CH is central heating

explanation.surface: A wife carefully regulates the central heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife, short for duchess.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch, from Cockney rhyming slang via duchess, is an informal term for one's spouse.

clue.text: Art produced by rich RCA tutee?

indicators.note: produced means made into something new, so these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: Art made by a wealthy student of the Royal College of Art.
explanation.walkthrough: RCA is the Royal College of Art in London; its student would study design, which supports the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture is the art and practice of designing buildings.

clue.text: Composer transposing parts in crib

indicators.note: swapping two portions of the word around means its halves change places

parts.note: a crib is a manger, a feeding trough

explanation.surface: A musician rearranges the pieces of a nativity scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transposing parts in' swaps MAN and GER in MANGER. Edward German was an English composer of light opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward German was an English composer, best known for the operetta Merrie England.

clue.text: Include points on circuit

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
compass means range or circuit, a bounded area

explanation.surface: Points on a circuit are covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circuit' looks like a racetrack, but here it means range or scope.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass is to contain or take in, as a survey takes in every topic.

clue.text: Bobby supporting staff for high-ranking official

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting below another piece

parts.note: to man is to staff a post
Bobby Darin was an American singer

explanation.surface: A policeman backs up the staff to help a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' looks like a British policeman, but it is the singer Bobby Darin.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a senior Chinese civil servant, and the word now means any powerful bureaucrat.

clue.text: Being short of wrapping length is irritating

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: needing something means being short of it

explanation.surface: Lacking enough wrapping paper is annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling means provoking or goading someone persistently.

clue.text: A cat is nervous about managing a complaint

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece
nervous suggests jittery movement, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: managing means in charge, abbreviated IC

explanation.surface: A jittery cat is fussing over an ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous' turns A CAT IS into SCIATA, and 'about' wraps that round IC. 'nervous' also plays on sciatica as a nerve complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sciatica is a painful ailment of the sciatic nerve, and complaint means an illness.

clue.text: Fine cake containing a bit of cinnamon

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a scone is a small baked cake

indicators.note: a bit of a word here means just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A baker praises a cake with a hint of spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective praising the cake, but it is the definition: at Oxford colleges a sconce was a penalty, a fine for breaking table etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Oxford college custom a sconce was a forfeit imposed for breaches of dining etiquette, a kind of penalty.

clue.text: Uprising about to supplant popular revival

indicators.note: to supplant means to take the place of, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: an insurrection is a revolt
in means popular or fashionable
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A rebellion is overturned and the old ways return.
explanation.walkthrough: In INSURRECTION, RE (about) takes the place of IN (popular).
explanation.definitionFit: Resurrection means a coming back to life, a renewal of something dead or dormant.

clue.text: Ability to reinforce a boundary

parts.note: touch means skill or deftness, as in a deft touch
to line a garment is to back it with extra fabric, strengthening it

explanation.surface: Someone has the knack of strengthening a perimeter fence.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby the touchline is the side boundary of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The touchline marks the side edge of a football or rugby pitch, the limit of play.

clue.text: Woody's ex, confronted by film classification, beginning to laugh and cry

parts.note: Mia Farrow was Woody Allen's former partner
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

indicators.note: the beginning of a word means its opening letter

explanation.surface: An actress meets the censor and goes from laughter to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: MIA (Farrow, Woody Allen's ex) plus U (a film rating) plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: To miaul is to mew like a cat, a plaintive sound.

clue.text: RU delegation organised relaxation of rules

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugby union delegation arranged for the rulebook to be loosened.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is Rugby Union, but here the letters are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Deregulation means removing official controls, loosening the restrictions on an industry.

clue.text: A question could generate corrections to compensate for errors

definitions.note: plural sense: in astronomy, personal equations are adjustments for an observer's errors

indicators.note: could generate suggests the letters can be made into something else

explanation.surface: A query might lead to amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: An observer's 'personal equation' is a correction applied for their habitual error in measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: In science, an equation can be an allowance added to offset systematic observational mistakes.

clue.text: What's a group of cells? It's on the tip of my tongue

definitions.text: It's on the tip of my tongue

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to recall a biology term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's on the tip of my tongue' usually means a word you cannot quite recall; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste receptor is a cluster of sensory cells, and these clusters are found on the surface of the tongue.

clue.text: Function involving extremists belonging to political party

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
NF is the National Front, a British far-right party
in means belonging to, as in in the club

explanation.surface: An event involving radicals is linked to a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' gives SINNFE. The National Front is a British far-right group, and 'Function' means the trigonometric sine, not an event.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinn Féin is an Irish republican political organisation.

clue.text: Beekeeper is a sanctimonious devotee of refined taste

parts.note: pi is informal for pious or sanctimonious
a culturist is someone devoted to culture and cultivated taste

explanation.surface: A beekeeper is described as a pious aesthete.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiculture is the keeping of bees, and its practitioner tends the hives.

clue.text: Maybe Dawn regularly stripped for Lenny Henry, grasping comic's bottom

indicators.note: grasping means holding inside, so one piece goes inside the other
stripping letters regularly removes every other one, keeping the first, third and so on

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Dawn stands in for Lenny Henry, holding on to the comic's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn French is a British comedian, once married to Lenny Henry; 'Henry' gives only H, the unit symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn French is an English comic actress, so the surname is an example of a Dawn.

clue.text: Back in a tick

explanation.surface: Someone promises to return shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to support it, and a moment is a brief instant of time.

clue.text: Doctrine initially expounded in tabernacle

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes into the other word

parts.note: a tabernacle was originally a tent, the portable sanctuary of the Israelites

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A preacher sets out a doctrine inside a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, especially by a group.

clue.text: Potential winner taking speed and heroin

parts.note: to race is to speed
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug-taking athlete hopes to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' and 'heroin' both look like drug slang; speed gives RACE, and horse is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred bred for the turf is a contender who might come first.

clue.text: Scavenger longing for the heart to laugh

indicators.note: being the heart of a word means sitting inside it

parts.note: ha is a laugh
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A scavenger yearns for a good laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The laughing hyena is known for its cackle, which ties the surface to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas feed on carrion, the remains of animals killed by others.

clue.text: Frenchman in stereotypical headgear suffering first European restriction

indicators.note: restriction means something is curtailed, here a letter is lost from the assembly

parts.note: the beret is the cap stereotypically worn by a Frenchman

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European; first says which E of the two goes
in, meaning wearing, can be read as on

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in a beret suffers the first of Europe's restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: BERET + ON (wearing) gives BERETON; losing its first E leaves BRETON, a man from Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: A Breton is a native of Brittany, a region of France, so a Frenchman.

clue.text: Overlook present of new toy that is incomplete

parts.note: to present is to give
o' is a short form of of

indicators.note: incomplete means missing its end, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a gift of an unfinished new toy.
explanation.walkthrough: TOY without its last letter is TO. A window that gives onto a garden overlooks it.
explanation.definitionFit: A room that faces a view, as in a window opening on a courtyard, is said to command it.

clue.text: Meal including a pastry

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dish is a course or meal
an is a form of the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: A meal includes a sweet pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish is a sweet flaky breakfast bun, short for Danish pastry.

clue.text: Third of cheques new accountant lost converted into money

indicators.note: third of a word here means its third letter

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
to shed is to lose

explanation.surface: An accountant mislaid a new batch of cheques that had been turned into cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The third letter of 'cheques' is E.
explanation.definitionFit: To encash is to cash a cheque, turning it into ready money.
